messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Change the video's camera setup to an upper-body shot from behind. Use the provided reference image to determine the viewing direction, subject placement, and framing at the start of the edited video. Retain the same person, hairstyle, hair color, outfit, expression, and action in the same environment. Only change how the camera captures the scene. Follow the camera setup and movement described above, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Retain the same person, hairstyle, hair color, outfit, expression, and action in the same environment. Only change how the camera captures the scene. Use the provided reference image to determine the viewing direction, subject placement, and framing at the start of the edited video. Follow the camera setup and movement described above, and preserve the timing and progression of the action in the source video.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The person stands facing away from the camera, then turns their head and upper body to the right, and finally returns to a forward-facing stance.","camera":"The camera maintains a static, medium shot from behind the subject at a slightly low angle.","clothing":"They are wearing a white sleeveless tank top with a large red and orange palm tree graphic on the back, paired with light green shorts.","hair_color":"The hair is dark brown or black.","hairstyle":"Their hair is pulled up into a high, somewhat messy bun or topknot.","identity":"A person with a medium build and dark skin is shown from behind, with their face not visible.","scene":"The setting is an outdoor paved area next to a body of water, with a clear blue sky and a wooden post visible in the background."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The output begins as a closer medium/upper-body rear shot, framing the subject from roughly the upper thighs/waist upward, matching the reference’s behind-the-subject direction and centered placement. The same person, bun, tank top, green shorts, seaside environment, and turning action are retained, with the action progression appearing similar to the source.
arguments.requested_change: Change the camera to an upper-body shot from behind, using the reference for initial direction, placement, and framing, while preserving the person, appearance, outfit, action, environment, and timing.
uncertain: Exact match of the opening framing to the reference image could not be verified pixel-for-pixel.
unexpected_changes: The lower legs and shoes are no longer visible in the new framing, as expected for an upper-body shot but a visible change from the source full-body framing.
